problem.headline: Five ways your site is quietly costing you deals
problem.bandText: If two of these sound familiar, the rest of this page is for you.

plates.heading: Your homepage explains what you built, not why anyone should care.
plates.body: Visitors land, skim, and leave — the layer that says why it matters was never built.

plates.heading: Marketing owns a website they can’t update without engineering.
plates.body: Every copy change rides a ticket through the dev queue. Two to six weeks, every time.

plates.heading: You redesigned six months ago and organic traffic still hasn’t moved.
plates.body: New design, same rankings — invisible to the buyers searching for what you sell.

plates.heading: Buyers ask ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Claude who to shortlist.
plates.body: The shortlist forms inside the answer — and it names your competitors, not you.

plates.heading: Your site gets traffic, but the conversion rate hasn’t changed in a year.
plates.body: Traffic without conversion is a vanity metric, and nobody is running experiments.

process.headline: How an engagement works
process.subtitle: No 47-slide proposals. No three-month discovery phases. Here’s what actually happens.

steps.title: Strategy call
steps.body: We talk for 30 minutes. You tell us what’s broken, what you’ve tried, and what good looks like. We tell you honestly whether we’re the right fit. If we are, we send a scope and timeline within 48 hours.

steps.title: Set the growth plan
steps.body: We audit discovery, content, conversion, and the current stack. Then we start the work with the clearest route to customers. If a site or page is the constraint, we scope the delivery work.

steps.title: Ship and measure
steps.body: We ship the agreed work, set up analytics where needed, and establish baseline metrics. No vanity dashboards. We track the numbers that connect to pipeline: organic traffic, conversion rates, form submissions, and qualified lead volume.

steps.title: Grow and optimize
steps.body: SEO, AEO, and CRO kick in. We publish content, optimize pages, and run conversion experiments. You get a monthly report with what we did, what moved, and what we’re doing next.

faq.headline: Before you book.
faq.lead: Straight answers to the questions every B2B SaaS team asks us. Everything else, bring to the call.

items.question: What types of companies do you work with?
items.answer: B2B SaaS companies, primarily Series A and later. Our clients typically have a product in market, a marketing team (even if it’s one person), and a website that isn’t pulling its weight. We’ve worked across verticals — fintech, healthtech, devtools, HR tech, cybersecurity — but the common thread is always B2B SaaS.

items.question: How do you choose the delivery stack?
items.answer: We start with the growth program, not a platform. Webflow is one delivery option when it fits the current site, team, and scope. We use another stack when it serves discovery, conversion, or operations better.

items.question: Can we start with one service?
items.answer: Yes. You can start with GEO, SEO, AEO, content, conversion, or a defined implementation project. We recommend the first scope after the audit. You can add work later when it supports the result.

items.question: How long does a website project take?
items.answer: Most builds go from kickoff to launch in 4-6 weeks. That includes strategy, copywriting, design, and Webflow development. Larger projects with complex CMS structures or multiple product lines can take 8-10 weeks. We’ll give you a specific timeline in the scoping call before you commit to anything.

items.question: What does the growth engagement look like month to month?
items.answer: We run SEO (technical and content), AEO (AI search optimization), and CRO (conversion experiments) on a monthly retainer. You get a dedicated team, weekly async updates, and a monthly performance review. We track organic traffic, keyword rankings, conversion rates, and qualified leads. Minimum engagement is three months — SEO needs at least that long to show meaningful results.

items.question: We already have a website. Can you optimize it without rebuilding?
items.answer: Sometimes. We can run SEO, AEO, and CRO on a stack we can work with efficiently. If the site is the bottleneck because it is slow, hard to update, or poorly structured for search, we will tell you. Then we scope only the delivery work that removes the constraint.

coverCta.headline: Let’s figure out what’s holding your site back.
coverCta.body: 30-minute strategy call. No pitch deck. We’ll look at your site together and tell you what we’d change and why.
